{{Quote|As you may know, the Sacred Circle is a religious order. On our home planet, Monastery, we worship the eternal, ever-renewing circle of life. We try to do so peacefully&hellip; far removed from the normal traffic and turmoil of the galaxy.|Domina Tagge|<ref name="marvel35" />}}
'''Monastery''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] that was home to the religious order known as the [[Order of the Sacred Circle]], who originally settled the world and ruled it for thousands of [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. Distinguished by its massive ring, Monastery had a number of dangerous native predators, and its topography itself could be deadly&mdash;for instance, the planet's [[Crystal Valley (Monastery)|Crystal Valley]] could mean certain [[Death/Legends|death]] to most visitors, as jagged [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]] burst from the ground without warning. Monastery remained cloistered and neutral from most [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] affairs throughout much of its history, but Sacred Circle [[Priest/Legends|priestess]] [[Domina Tagge/Legends|Domina Tagge]] brought it into [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] intrigues during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], it hosted a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] [[Mission to Monastery|duel]] between [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] hero [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and Tagge's brother [[Orman Tagge/Legends|Orman]], which Skywalker won in deadly fashion.

==Description==
{{Quote|T- that crystal&hellip;! Seemed to burst from the ground! Moisture from this heavy drew and mist must cause some sort of chemical reaction&mdash;makes them grow fast&hellip; almost explosively!|Luke Skywalker, attempting to traverse Monastery's dangerous Crystal Valley|<ref name="marvel37" />}}
[[File:CrystalValley-SW1977-37.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Luke Skywalker attempts to navigate the treacherous Crystal Valley.]]
Located along the [[Reena Trade Route]] in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim's]]<ref name="TEA" /> [[Haserian sector/Legends|Haserian sector]]&mdash;<ref name="EAOC" /> between [[Haseria system/Legends|Haseria]] and [[Masterra]]&mdash;<ref name="TEA" /> the ringed [[Planet/Legends|planet]] Monastery was covered in vast [[Forest/Legends|rainforests]] that housed a number of fierce predators.<ref name="marvel35" /> Among the dangerous beasts that called Monastery's forests was the deadly [[saber cat]], which was often tamed by the [[Order of the Sacred Circle]] pilgrims who settled the world,<ref name="unknown" /> as well as the imposing, avian [[nightshrike]].<ref name="marvel35" /> Outside the planet's rainforests, Monastery's topography tended towards the bizarre and inhospitable. One example was the deadly [[Crystal Valley (Monastery)|Crystal Valley]], where ever-present moisture and dew caused chemical reactions within the soil that prompted massive, jagged [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]] to burst from the ground with no warning.<ref name="marvel37" />

==History==
{{Quote|It was devastating enough to be dumped from their homeworlds like out-of-season sandals, but to end up on such dismally dull worlds as Naboo and Monastery?|Dyslogia Twang, during the Separatist crisis|<ref name="HNN53">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|53|life/13425_1.html|SPECIAL FEATURE: Sightings by Twang}}</ref>}}
Like many worlds in the Mid Rim, Monastery was colonized as a religious haven, originally being settled by the Order of the Sacred Circle. The Order wholly owned the planet for almost its entire history,<ref name="TEA" /> using Monastery as the center of its worship of the ever-renewing circle of life.<ref name="marvel35" /> By the era of the [[Great Galactic War]], Monastery's pilgrims had become known for techniques of relaxation and concentration that attracted students from across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="suns">[[The Old Republic — The Lost Suns 4|''The Old Republic — The Lost Suns'' 4]]</ref> In [[3661 BBY]],<ref name="date">In [[The Old Republic — The Lost Suns 4|''The Old Republic—The Lost Suns 4'']], Theron Shan mentions that Ngani Zho took him to Monastery at the age of five. ''[[The Old Republic: Annihilation]]'' sets Shan's birth year at [[3666 BBY]], meaning that he visited Monastery around 3661 BBY.</ref> the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Ngani Zho]] brought his young charge, future [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Spy/Legends|spy]] [[Theron Shan]], to Monastery to learn better focus. Shan remained on the world for a [[Standard year/Legends|year]] and a half, during which time he learned to ignore all pain and distractions, before he left the service of the Order of the Sacred Circle.<ref name="suns" />

The Order's hold on Monastery continued for millennia, through the era of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]<ref name="HNN52" /> and the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="marvel35" /> In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Monastery was one of [[Refugee Relief Movement/Legends|10 Mid Rim worlds]] to loosen immigration restrictions in the wake of the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], although it required all incoming citizens to surrender all weapons and convert to the Order of the Sacred Circle. According to census records posted on [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]], 35 million refugees immigrated to Monastery.<ref name="HNN52" /> Monastery officially remained neutral throughout the early stages of the Galactic Civil War, but by that time the Order had come under the control of [[Priestess/Legends|Priestess]] [[Domina Tagge/Legends|Domina Tagge]], who involved the planet in [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] intrigues around [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]]. A member of the wealthy and powerful [[House of Tagge/Legends|House of Tagge]], Tagge was contacted by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], who claimed to her that her elder brothers [[Orman Tagge/Legends|Orman]] and [[Silas Tagge/Legends|Silas Tagge]] had [[Death/Legends|died]] at the hands of [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] hero [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], the destroyer of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]]. Wanting revenge, Tagge lured Skywalker to Monastery, inviting him to present the Rebel Alliance's case for the Order's support&mdash;Vader was there waiting, ostensibly as the Empire's representative in the bidding.<ref name="marvel35" />

[[File:Monastery.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Domina Tagge, Luke Skywalker and Darth Vader overlook Monastery's Crystal Valley.]]
At Tagge's request, Skywalker [[Mission to Monastery|traveled to Monastery]] alone, although his friends [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] followed behind in case he needed help.<ref name="marvel35" /> But when Skywalker arrived at the [[Temple of the Sacred Circle]] to plead the Rebel Alliance's case, he found a vengeful Tagge denouncing him and the Rebellion, and Vader, smirking under his [[Darth Vader's armor/Legends|mask]], challenging him to a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|duel]]. Skywalker accepted, but Tagge would not permit them to battle in the temple, instead forcing them to fight in the dangerous Crystal Valley.<ref name="marvel36">[[Star Wars (1977) 36|''Star Wars'' (1977) 36]]</ref> Tagge hoped that the valley's unpredictable topography would eliminate both combatants&mdash;although she had worked with Vader, he was a long-time rival of her beloved brother Orman, and she held him considerable ill will. However, their descent into the valley was interrupted by none other than Orman Tagge, who had in fact survived the catastrophic [[Battle of the Corridor]] and had, until recently, been kept in [[Stasis booth|stasis]] aboard Vader's [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]]. Orman had found his way aboard Solo's ''[[Millennium Falcon/Legends|Millennium Falcon]]'' and forced it to land on Monastery: he had only revenge on Vader on his mind.<ref name="marvel37" />

But without [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to guide him, Tagge had little chance of navigating the Crystal Valley successfully. Vader saved his life from a falling crystal, but in return forced Tagge to battle Skywalker in his stead, disguised as the Sith Lord through use of [[Mind trick/Legends|illusion]]. Skywalker bested and slew the [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] of House Tagge in single combat, but fled another encounter with Vader and departed the planet with the Rebels. The saga ended Domina Tagge's reign over the Order of the Sacred Circle, and afterward, Monastery continued to remain neutral in the Galactic Civil War.<ref name="marvel37" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|Monastery is a cloistered world&hellip; usually not open to visitors.|Domina Tagge|<ref name="marvel35" />}}
[[File:Temple_of_the_Sacred_Circle.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Order of the Sacred Circle mainly resided inside its Temple, located among the planet's verdant rainforests.]]
By [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Monastery had an official population of approximately 35 million, of which all were members of the Order of the Sacred Circle&mdash;incoming residents were required to join the religion,<ref name="HNN52" /> although the planet had been more open to curious outsiders interested in learning the Order's teachings in the past.<ref name="suns" /> By the era of the Galactic Civil War, the planet was cloistered, and generally did not permit visitors unless they were specifically invited by the Order.<ref name="marvel35" />

==Locations==
{{Quote|The Temple of the Sacred Circle&hellip;! It is where we worship and abide.|Domina Tagge|<ref name="marvel35" />}}
The center of the Order of the Sacred Circle was located in Monastery's opulent Temple of the Sacred Circle, which housed most of the Order's membership amidst the planet's dense rainforests.<ref name="marvel35" /> As according with the Order's policy of nonviolence, fighting was not permitted within the temple&mdash;in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], Luke Skywalker and Darth Vader were instead forced to fight in the nearby Crystal Valley, one of the most dangerous features of Monastery's landscape, where deadly crystals blasted through the planet's surface with no warning.<ref name="marvel37" />

==Behind the scenes==
Monastery first appeared in [[Star Wars (1977) 35|''Star Wars'' (1977) 35]], written by [[Archie Goodwin]] and released in [[1980]]. The planet went on to be featured as the main setting of the next two issues of the [[Star Wars (1977)|Marvel ''Star Wars'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series, during which time it was illustrated by [[Carmine Infantino]].<ref name="marvel35" /><ref name="marvel36" /><ref name="marvel37" /> The planet was occasionally misspelled "Monastary" in several later sources, namely ''[[HoloNet News Vol. 531 #52]]'', where it is spelled correctly and incorrectly just paragraphs apart.<ref name="HNN52" />
